Increase separation enough for the court/seam to be visibly read across views.
Keep the split legible and avoid collapsing the void back into a generic block.
Align the entry cut with the verified access edge.
Broaden the notch so the street response becomes a clear ground-level invitation.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant mass from a compact block toward a split-wing/courtyard-like organization that better supports a public void without losing the main body.
Open a more legible seam so the ground plane can read as occupied public space rather than a sealed object.
Keep the mass from fully rejoining so the void remains intentional and publicly readable.
Bind the public threshold to the verified access side.
Enlarge the access cut so it registers as a real entry seam or public bite at ground level.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass in all four views, so it passes basic cross-view consistency, but it is still close to a generic compressed box with faceted setbacks. The parcel relationship is only moderately successful: the form sits within the green boundary and does not obviously ignore it, yet the dominant gesture does not strongly organize itself around the site shape. The verified access edge is answered only weakly; the blue frontage is adjacent to the mass, but the ground response is more of a clipped edge than a legible public threshold, court, or entry seam. The silhouette is coherent but not especially program-bearing; the stepped/faceted top is acceptable as massing, though not as a strong section idea. For neighborhood living, the form needs clearer active-ground logic and a more explicit void/public threshold to feel programmatically convincing.
